finding.claim: GET /rss passes the unvalidated user-supplied query parameter u directly to URI.open, letting an unauthenticated attacker make the server fetch any URL (internal hosts, cloud metadata) and return the first 400 bytes of the response.
finding.source: params[:u] (query parameter u on GET /rss), app.rb:7-8, unauthenticated

trace.note: params[:u] passed directly to URI.open with no parse, host, scheme, or allowlist check; .read fetches the response
data[0, 400] returns only the first 400 bytes, limiting exfiltration but not what is fetched

finding.guards_checked: None on this path. Only the 400-byte truncation at app.rb:9, which limits returned data but not the request target. URI.open follows HTTP redirects, so no first-URL check would hold either. Compare with /trusted (app.rb:13-14), which does validate the host; /rss has no equivalent.

verdict.guard_found: none. app.rb:7-9 has no validation before the sink. The only check in the file is the TRUSTED host allowlist at app.rb:13-14, which is in the separate /trusted route and does not apply to /rss.
verdict.reason: The `/rss` route at app.rb:7 takes `params[:u]` with no authentication and passes it unvalidated to `URI.open(...)` at app.rb:8, which fetches the URL and follows redirects; app.rb:9 truncates the output to 400 bytes but does not restrict the request target, so the SSRF stands.
